quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing signals or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Only cross when your entire vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle may stall.

questions.question: If you are convicted of DUII for the first time, how long will your license be suspended?

options.text: Six months
Three months
One year
Two years

questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: A first DUII conviction results in a one-year license suspension.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Overcorrect.
Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Release the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm and steer in the direction the vehicle is skidding.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your ability to stop. Slow down on poor or slippery roads to maintain control of your vehicle and avoid accidents.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete your turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the direction you came from. This keeps your turn smooth and safe.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far your vehicle takes to stop?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These factors change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may take up to ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers need more distance to stop than regular cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph can take almost 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: When you increase your vehicle's speed:

options.text: Your field of vision increases.
Your field of vision decreases.
It is easier to see cross traffic.
Your field of vision does not change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your field of vision decreases.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, stay extra alert to spot potential hazards.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Use your mirrors and turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you use?

options.text: The lane closest to where you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.
questions.explanation: Stop parallel to the vehicle in front of your desired parking space. Check traffic and signal first. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: By driving a motor vehicle in Oregon, you have agreed to:

options.text: Keep liability insurance for as long as you drive.
Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
Post bail or go to court if arrested for a traffic violation.
Keep your vehicle's equipment in safe working condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
questions.explanation: Oregon's Implied Consent Law says that by driving, you agree to take a breath, blood, or urine test if a police officer asks after arresting you for driving under the influence. Refusing the test has serious legal consequences.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a bicycle crossing or path. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles often cross or ride near traffic here.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you has broken down.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: When changing lanes to the left, where should you look to check your blind spot?

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass. Only pass if you can do so safely and legally.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Mean your vehicle needs a tune-up sooner than usual.
Make you feel sleepy while driving.
Start fires in grass on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from the engine, reduces noise, and cools hot gases. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system are dangerous and can kill you quickly. They can also make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are good.
The suggested speed to drive on a road when conditions are good.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are good. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when bad weather or road construction make the posted speed unsafe.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to cross after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, check for another train on the other track before crossing.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check for another train on the other track before crossing.
questions.explanation: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross the tracks until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic is moving in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic is moving in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed lines mean drivers next to the line can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this hand signal.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing the lanes. You may:

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never cross these lines.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows that the road has a sharp curve in the direction of the arrow (to the left). You may see several chevron signs placed along the curve.

questions.question: When a car ahead has bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car comes toward you with bright headlights on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should adjust when you get into a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel after your seat is in the right position.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up to alert people nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Before you get in to back up, walk around to the back and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show directions and distances to places. They help drivers who are unfamiliar with an area.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: When driving on curves, the most important thing is to:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may be hard to turn due to its forward motion. Slow down before entering a curve so you can keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. Children are playing nearby. What should you do before you start moving?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Look through your back window when backing up. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially around children. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing out of a driveway.
